body:
Some relevant background from earlier discussions:

- In February 2024, [s1na explicitly supported specifying optional APIs](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/804019759934078987/1207296052080672828), using `trace_` as the example: most clients implement it, Geth does not, and the shared behavior remains unspecified. In the preceding discussion, [fjl noted that there was no official optional status](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/804019759934078987/1205596766477488209). These were proposals and observations at the time, rather than an adopted conformance policy.
- In December 2025, [Chase described preparatory work for adding methods such as `trace_block` and `trace_transaction`](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/804019759934078987/1452695599207153706), alongside the separate `debug_trace*` standardization effort. The corresponding Hive change, [ethereum/hive#1378](https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1378), merged and enabled the `trace` namespace on supporting clients. That provides infrastructure groundwork, though it does not itself specify these methods or establish an optional profile.

Is there an existing plan or unresolved blocker from that work that this issue should align with? In particular, it would help to understand the intended conformance model for methods implemented by only some clients. We can contribute discrepancy reports and regression fixtures from the evm-trace investigation, including cases where compressed `vmTrace` output cannot reliably reconstruct execution state.
Thanks for raising this, adding it to the RPC Standards call agenda for next Monday.

Hey @banteg - I'll be as transparent and blunt as I can be.

I support the standardization of the "Parity" `trace_` namespace. Historically, the blocker has always been the go-ethereum team. They have refused to add the namespace and the methods to go-ethereum in the past. With that said, many of the team members who opposed it are not maintainers anymore and I have spoken to some other members of the team who are in favor of adding support.

If it was completely up to me, tracers would be removed from the `debug` namespace entirely. Mixing tracer methods with dangerous methods like `debug_setHead` is, and always was, a terrible design decision.

Putting that aside, there are a few way I could see this going.

First and foremost we need a spec, ideally that spec would be clean across the clients that already support the method: Nethermind, Erigon, Reth, etc. such that we have a rough consensus among those clients and a baseline to test go-ethereum with. This could come in the form of a PR to this repo without tests to accompany it.

I do not know if all the other clients are in 100% agreement and conformance with the trace methods today, but a simple hivechain cross client test could give us the answer. If they're not, someone will have to decide what is "correct" and what is not, and create the upstream fixes to get them in agreement.

Once that is done, then we either need to:

A. Implement it in go-ethereum and generate the tests for this repo via testgen
...or...
B. Bypass go-ethereum, bypass the test files, and merge it without tests

I'm fairly confident that if we can propose the spec, get all the client teams to thumbs up (why wouldn't they if they already pass the spec with working implementations?) that the go-ethereum team would come on board.

A small update ahead of the call: we now have reproducible cases showing that the remaining differences extend beyond method signatures.

On Reth v2.5.2, read-only simulations show EIP-7702 delegation changes reported as unchanged in `stateDiff.code`, and constructor/delegated execution returning missing or stale `vmTrace.code`. These are trace-output problems; the simulated execution produces the expected results. So far these reproductions are on Reth only, rather than a completed cross-client comparison.

We've also prepared a diagnostic fixture set covering selector/filter semantics and output fidelity, with observed behavior separated from proposed expectations. Happy to contribute those once the group agrees on scope and the conformance/testing approach.

I think your best best in getting the tracers standardized and merged into this repo is to focus on what the majority of clients support today, if say 4 out of 6 clients support the method and more or less agree on the output the less we have to argue about the spec and the more likely it is we can include it as canonical here.

The easiest way to figure that out is to just run hive's rpc-compat tests with hand written test files and identifying the diffs across clients. I'm sure Claude or Codex could knock that out in like an hour.

hive now has https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1587 which was created for testing callTracer, it should help here in generating useful calls to test against.

Also, I have an AI skill for this type of work, if you're interested in taking a stab at it:
https://github.com/MysticRyuujin/rpcwright

Following @MysticRyuujin's suggestion, we ran Hive's rpc-compat tests against Erigon, Nethermind, Reth and Besu on the same small generated chain. There is shared behavior to build on, but some basic contracts need agreement: `trace_get` with an empty path returns a root object, null or an array depending on the client, and default `trace_filter` matching across sender/recipient lists splits OR (Erigon/Reth) versus AND (Nethermind/Besu).

We also reproduced reporting bugs, including missing precompile return bytes in Besu's call-frame result and omitted EIP-7702 code changes in Reth's replay `stateDiff`. I've collected the [findings and suggested resolutions here](https://gist.github.com/banteg/d32a87ed2c47dfa4dbf1958235f8bf82). The recommendations are provisional; runnable fixtures are ready to contribute once we agree on scope and testing approach.

The findings are significant, in that there's a lot of them, all of which would have to get resolved in the clients.

The doc you produced has seemingly sensible recommendations and explanations for those decisions.

The next step would be to write the actual spec yaml, resolving as many of the discrepancies as possible. Followed by draft PRs (or issues) to the clients aligning them with the proposed spec.

This would allow each client team to respond to the spec and evaluate the necessary changes to comply.

An update on this: I've put together a [draft specification](https://github.com/banteg/execution-apis/tree/feat/trace) and a [cross-client test harness](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop) covering all nine `trace_*` methods, including `trace`, `stateDiff` and `vmTrace`.

Following the suggestions here, there are now [per-client reports](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/tree/main/reports/clients) for Erigon, Reth, Nethermind and Besu. Each report explains the observed differences, proposed behavior, and what would need to change, with runnable cases and links to the relevant client code. The [decision ledger](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/decisions/README.md) collects the open questions and rationale. These are proposals for review; where a client disagrees with the draft, either side could need changing.

I've also implemented the namespace in an experimental [Geth branch](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/tree/feat/trace), tested against the same harness. This gives us a concrete implementation to discuss with the Geth team, though it isn't upstream support or endorsement. Some independent reporting fixes have already been submitted upstream; their status is tracked [here](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/docs/client-fixes.md).

The next step is to work through the disagreements with client maintainers and prepare manageable patches alongside any revisions to the spec. It would help to have one person from each client team own that review: start with your client's report, challenge the proposed choices, and help settle the behavior and compatibility implications.

I've set up a [Telegram working group](https://t.me/+2jfwc-YvwkliMzIy) for coordination. Please join or point someone from your team to it if you'd like to work on this. We can keep decisions and their rationale here and in the spec review so they're publicly reviewable.

For H03/H13, Erigon agrees with the direction on both. A few notes on each

  **H03**
  - AND as the default, and unrecognized mode values rejected.
  - The AND default restores OpenEthereum's semantics: an empty list matches everything, and the two sides are combined with AND. In Erigon the AND case is already expressible with mode: "intersection" (erigontech/erigon#2119), so the change flips the default without removing anything: whoever wants union can keep asking for it explicitly.
  - On compatibility: the only request whose behavior changes is one that supplies both lists and no mode. The case to document is {fromAddress: [X], toAddress: [X]}, written to mean "all activity involving X": under AND it becomes "calls from X to X", so it returns almost nothing, and no error. The migration is one field, mode: "union" — which is also why we ask that the
    extension stays.
  - We also ask that mode: "intersection" remains a valid value, as a no-op under the new default: it is what users who already needed AND send today, and they would be the only ones to break if it became an unsupported value.
  
  **H13**
  - Agreed, but we would widen it to "apply the full admission rules at the selected state": the nonce is one case, and the same path also skips the balance check and EIP-3607.
  - Some context: the check is absent in OpenEthereum as well as in Nethermind, Besu and Erigon — OE did not validate the nonce and topped up the sender's balance. We support the change anyway, because without the check the CREATE address and the stateDiff nonce are derived from the state nonce, so they describe a different transaction.
  - One consequence to keep in mind if the optional blockNumber field that OpenEthereum had is ever restored: with the check in place, tracing a transaction at a past block becomes harder, because the caller has to know in advance the nonce the sender had at that block — and if it does not match there is no remedy, since the transaction is signed. The exception is pointing
    at the exact block the transaction belonged to, where the nonce matches on its own. The two decisions stay separate, but they interact.
  - Please settle the error code along with the policy: rejections are -32000 here and -32000/-32003 in Reth.

An update since the draft went up.

**The draft changed.** A [source review](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/docs/source-review/README.md) compared the draft with the Parity source, current Besu/Erigon/Nethermind/Reth code and the sibling `eth_*` methods, and its recommendations are now in [#895](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/895). The larger changes:

- `trace_filter` range errors follow `eth_getLogs` (#875): a bound beyond the head, a reversed range or `pending` returns `-32602`, with no clamping.
- Failed frames (H09): a REVERT frame carries `result: {gasUsed, output}`, as Erigon and Reth already emit; a failed CREATE reports no address or code; other halts may omit `result`. Failure labels are a fixed list.
- vmTrace `mem` (H20) is the post-operation contents of the range the opcode's operands designate, including MLOAD and the full CALL output window. This reverses the earlier "written bytes" narrowing and matches Parity, Erigon, Nethermind and Besu for MLOAD.
- Unsigned calls (H15) take their fee defaults and zero-fee BASEFEE rule from `eth_call`/`eth_simulateV1`, and gas above the RPC cap runs at the cap as `eth_call` does.
- Error codes reuse existing conventions: `eth_simulateV1` codes for `trace_call`/`trace_callMany`, and the `eth_sendRawTransaction` error groups for `trace_rawTransaction`.
- New rules for frame gas fields, calls that fail their precheck, callMany item boundaries, stateDiff existence and markers, and vmTrace gas at call boundaries, where the draft was previously silent.

@lupin012, on your H03/H13 notes: `mode: "intersection"` remains valid as the default, and the H13 codes are now settled together with the policy, using the error groups above with `-32003` as the fallback. The block-argument interaction you describe is recorded under H12, which stays an extension.

**Client progress.** Eleven more fixes are open across [Besu, Erigon, Nethermind, Reth and revm-inspectors](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/docs/client-fixes.md), and Reth #27423 has merged. The [decision index](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/decisions/README.md) now marks 🛠️ where a submitted fix covers the whole measured difference, so the remaining ⚠️ cells are unaddressed work. H02, H07, H18 and H26 are converged through merged client fixes, alongside H03, H13 and H28. The experimental Geth fork follows the revised draft with no differences in the current matrix.

The reorg scenario also found two Engine API bugs outside the trace namespace: Erigon [#24292](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/24292) (a same-head forkchoice update drops safe/finalized, which now blocks valid reorgs) and Reth [#27429](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27429) (a stale on-disk head is treated as canonical after a reorg).

**Where input would help most:**
- Client positions on the changed rules above, especially H09, H20 and the error codes. Each [client report](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/reports/README.md) lists what would change for that client.
- Could a maintainer approve the pending workflows on #895, so the proposal files can be validated?

Heads-up before a coordinated change to failed-frame output in `trace_*`, since it changes a wire shape that indexers may parse.

**Reverted CREATE result (H09).** Clients report a CREATE that reverts in three different ways today:

| | Reverted CREATE `result` |
| --- | --- |
| Erigon, Reth (revm-inspectors), Anvil | `{address: <would-be address>, code: <revert bytes>, gasUsed}` |
| Besu, Nethermind, Parity | none |
| Geth `flatCallTracer` | `{gasUsed, code}` |

The draft specifies `{gasUsed, output}`, exactly what a reverted CALL already returns: the frame's gas and its revert bytes, with no `address` and no `code`. No contract exists at the would-be address, and the revert bytes are not deployed code. In Erigon and revm-inspectors the current shape comes from the success serializer being reused for reverts, not from a separate decision, and no test locks it. Alloy already decodes `{gasUsed, output}` on a create action.

**Filter consequence (H23).** Because the draft's result has no address, `trace_filter` no longer matches a failed CREATE by its would-be address. It still matches its creator through `fromAddress`. Erigon, Nethermind and Reth match the would-be address today; Besu and the Geth draft do not.

**Failure labels.** The same PRs map failures to Parity's labels, so callers don't have to match client-specific strings: "Reverted", "Out of gas" (including code-size and code-deposit failures), "Bad instruction", "Bad jump destination", "Stack underflow", "Out of stack", "Mutable Call In Static Context", "Built-in failed", "Out of bounds", "Invalid code" for a 0xEF prefix, plus "Contract address collision", "Nonce overflow", "Insufficient balance for transfer" and "Max call depth exceeded". Today these range from Rust enum names (`CallTooDeep`, `CreateCollision`) to raw Go errors and Nethermind's own labels.

I have PRs ready for Erigon, revm-inspectors and Nethermind, and will open them in a couple of days unless someone prefers keeping the would-be address. The alternative is to standardize on `{address, code, gasUsed}` and let `trace_filter` keep matching it. Evidence and per-client tables: [H09](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/reports/decisions/H09.md), [H23](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/reports/decisions/H23.md), [review](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-09-26-divergent-decisions/H06-H09.md).

**Open question: `null` or an error for a missing transaction (H06)**

Nethermind objects to the draft's `null` for `trace_transaction`/`trace_get` of an unknown hash and prefers meaningful not-found errors. The draft's `null` isn't new: it's Parity's behavior, what Erigon and Reth return today (Besu for `trace_get`), and it matches `eth_getTransactionByHash`.

The strongest argument for an error is from the caller's side. A `null` reads as a definitive "nothing here", so the caller gives up. An error like "history unavailable, lookup inconclusive" tells them to try an archive node. With pruned history a node often can't tell a transaction that never existed from one it no longer indexes. The draft already returns 4444 when pruned indexing prevents establishing absence, but that only covers part of the problem.

Two options:
1. Keep `null` only when the node can prove absence (a complete transaction index), and return an error whenever it can't. This is close to the current draft, with the "can't prove it" case made general.
2. Return an error for every miss, with a dedicated not-found code. Nethermind's preference.

Erigon, Reth and Besu: which would you accept? Evidence and per-client behavior: [H06](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/reports/decisions/H06.md).

For comparison, `eth_getTransactionByHash` for an unknown hash (static read of current main in each client):

| | Unknown hash | When the lookup can't be sure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| execution-apis schema | `notFound` (null) | not specified |
| Geth | null once the tx index is complete | -32000 "transaction indexing is in progress" while it isn't ([api.go](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/920c07774c65ebb3023536f85df642c44478b540/internal/ethapi/api.go)) |
| Erigon | null | pruned-history error when the lookup finds the tx in a pruned block ([eth_txs.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/5f59ece1667/rpc/jsonrpc/eth_txs.go)) |
| Nethermind, Reth, Besu | null | none, every miss is null |

No client errors on a provable miss, and Geth already ships option 1: null when absence is provable, an error when the lookup is inconclusive. Whatever `trace_*` settles on, it would be good for `eth_getTransactionByHash` to follow the same rule.

I think hash based requests are a bit tricky and a `null` response is perhaps the least bad one, especially since most already do this already, so keeping it like that seems reasonable and wouldn't introduce new behaviour that applications need to handle

@banteg
Erigon's view on **H06**: the trace methods should answer the way our eth_* methods already answer the same question, with one rule per state.

  - A missing entity returns null. eth_getBlockByNumber and eth_getTransactionByHash both do, in our case with an explicit comment pointing at erigontech/erigon#1645. By that rule: a missing transaction, a missing trace path, and an unknown selected block.
  - A query that ran and matched nothing returns [].
  - A bad range returns -32602, as eth_getLogs does after ethereum/execution-apis#875 and as we already do there.
  - Pruned history returns an error, never a fake absence.

  We already apply the last rule in the trace namespace. On a node that has pruned its history — full or minimal — checkPruneHistory and checkBlockHistoryAvailable refuse the request instead of answering as if the data were simply absent: they guard six call sites in trace_adhoc.go and the trace_filter path, and the debug_* methods do the same. What is missing is a
  distinguishable code: state.PrunedError carries no RPC code, so those refusals surface as a generic -32000, and the only place we emit 4444 is the block-access-list helper.

  One thing worth reconciling in the draft: the case for null on a missing transaction is that eth_getTransactionByHash does it, but an unknown selected block is proposed as -32001, where eth_getBlockByNumber returns null. Either the eth_* analogy settles both, or the criterion is something else — and it would help to say which, since that is what the rest of the argument rests on.

@lupin012 thanks, that's the right question. The criterion isn't the `eth_*` analogy by itself. It's the one @mattsse suggested: grandfather in whatever the clients already agree on, and only choose where they differ.

- **Missing transaction or trace path → `null`.** Parity did it, Erigon and Reth do it today (Besu for `trace_get`), and it matches `eth_getTransactionByHash` everywhere.
- **Unknown selected block → error.** For `trace_block`, all four clients already return an error (Reth -32001, the others -32000), and none returns `null`. `trace_call` and `trace_callMany` error on an unknown block too, as `eth_call` does. Switching `trace_block` to `null` to mirror `eth_getBlockByNumber` would change every client for no caller asking for it.
- **`trace_replayBlockTransactions`** is the one real split: Besu and Reth return `null`, Erigon and Nethermind an error. I'd follow `trace_block` there, since both take the same block selector.

On the code, I'll relax the draft to "an error, -32001 recommended" rather than insist on one code. Your other three rules (`[]` for no matches, -32602 for a bad range, an error for pruned history) are already what the draft says. A distinguishable pruned-history code (4444) would help Erigon's `checkPruneHistory` refusals, but that can come later.

@banteg
Agreed on the criterion — grandfathering what clients already do and choosing only on real splits is the right rule for this, and it settles the block case better than the eth_* analogy did.

  On trace_replayBlockTransactions: Erigon errors today, so following trace_block keeps us unchanged and we prefer that to switching to null. Both methods take the same block selector, and a caller that has to branch on which one it called to know what "not there" looks like is worse off.

  We will move our unknown-block error to -32001 and give the pruned refusals a distinguishable code on our side — both are small and on our list, no need to hold the draft for them

@banteg 
On **H20**: the reversal matches what Erigon already does, so no change for us — MLOAD records the 32-byte range at the operand offset read after the operation, and a call records the caller's full declared output window rather than only the bytes written. Our remaining divergence on H20 is the part #24344 addresses.

On **H14**: we agree with the direction. On our side it is mostly wiring — the eth_simulateV1 code mapping already exists in Erigon but only that method uses it, so the trace paths surface as -32000 today. What would still need adding is the -32003 fallback, -32602 for malformed input, and unknown-field rejection in filter requests.
  One consistency point for the draft: if trace_rawTransaction adopts the eth_sendRawTransaction groups, our own eth_sendRawTransaction should follow, otherwise the same rejection carries two codes in one daemon. It would help if the mapping were stated as one table a client can implement once for both namespaces.

@banteg 
 **H09 / H23 — reverted CREATE.** Erigon currently emits `result: {address, code, gasUsed}` with `error: "Reverted"`, where `code` holds the revert returndata rather than deployed bytecode and `address` names a contract that does not exist. H23 removes the address, H09 removes the code, and a reverted CREATE is then left with nowhere to carry its revert data, while a
  reverted CALL keeps it in `output`.

  Our proposal: the same shape as a reverted CALL, `result: {gasUsed, output}` with `error: "Reverted"` next to it. The error field stays the signal that the frame failed, so dropping the address costs the consumer nothing. It also matches EIP-211, where the returndata buffer is populated only when a create reverts.

  | create outcome | `result` | `error` |
  |---|---|---|
  | success | `{address, code, gasUsed}` | absent |
  | revert | `{gasUsed, output}` | `"Reverted"` |
  | other halt (out of gas, invalid opcode, …) | `null` | the halt message |

@banteg
H15. Erigon agrees with the fee defaults (omitted fees 0, an unpriced call running with GASPRICE, BASEFEE and BLOBBASEFEE 0, GASLIMIT the block's, an omitted gas running at the RPC cap, a priced call paying for its gas). Fix PRs are already open on our side

@banteg
Should eth_getLogs and trace_filter accept the same bound types? Which would you prefer: reject hash bounds, allow them as an optional canonical-only extension, or require them?
Agreed: trace_filter should take the same bound types as eth_getLogs, so no hash bounds. The cost of keeping them is already visible on our side — reviewing #24357, awskii found that the same block past the executed head returns -32602 by number and -32000 by hash.
One open question comes with it. eth_getLogs rejects hashes in the range but still accepts a single block by hash, through a blockHash member that is mutually exclusive with the bounds. EIP-234 added it because a numeric query cannot tell an empty block from the wrong one: if a reorg lands between reading a block and asking for its logs, that height now holds a different block and an empty result is ambiguous. Traces are no different.

  Without that member there is no single call that pins the block by hash and filters by address at the same time: trace_filter by number keeps the filter but loses the pinning, trace_block keeps neither (it takes a number, and has no address lists, mode or paging), and trace_replayBlockTransactions keeps the pinning but has no filter and a different output shape. Should trace_filter get the member, so the two methods are actually aligned?

  Either answer works for us; but let's decide how to proceed on the single blockHash rather than leave it open

@lupin012 agreed, and thanks for raising it. Proposal: trace_filter gets `blockHash`, as eth_getLogs has since EIP-234.

- Mutually exclusive with fromBlock/toBlock (-32602 recommended); an explicit null counts as omitted.
- Selects exactly that block. Records carry its hash, and address matching, mode, rewards and after/count work as for a single-block range.
- One narrowing against EIP-234: canonical only. An unknown, non-canonical or not-yet-executed hash is an error (-32001 recommended), never `[]` or another block's records. Resolve the hash and trace in one view. Serving side-chain blocks would be a separate, later decision.
- Hash range bounds stay rejected, so `{fromBlock: H, toBlock: H}` becomes `{blockHash: H}`. That also settles the #24357 split: a bound past the head gets the range error, a hash outside the view the not-found error.

We measured it. Today nobody implements the member, and Besu, Erigon and Nethermind silently answer `{blockHash: H}` with the head block's traces, including for an unknown hash and, in the reorg run, for a replaced block. Reth, Anvil and the Geth fork reject it with -32602. For Erigon the change should be a small mapping onto `resolveLogsBlockHash`/`resolveCommittedBlockNumber` inside the existing transaction.

- Study with per-client source and evidence: https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-09-29-trace-filter-blockhash.md
- Tracked as H33: https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/blob/main/reports/decisions/H33.md

If canonical-only works for you, I'll add it to the draft.
